body:
Found while landing bloxwap/monorepo#4606 (#110), which replaced #4601. Evidence: automated browser runs on macOS and the monorepo CI.

## What happens

Firefox can't launch on the monorepo's Mac mini runners (bloxwap/monorepo#4603), so `tooling/hig/marketing-sections.mjs` and `tooling/hig/app-flows/browser.mjs` were ported to take `HIG_BROWSER=chromium|webkit`.

`HIG_BROWSER=webkit node tooling/hig/app-flows/browser.mjs` passes about 30–40 feedback cases, then `page.goto` hits its 30 s timeout. The case it stops on differs between runs. It reproduces locally on macOS.

- Each page loads fine on its own.
- `Connection: close` on the fixture server did not help.
- On CI the hang held the HIG web job for 40 minutes.

So `.github/workflows/hig-quality.yml` runs app-flows in **Chrome only** (notes in that file and in `docs/hig/pilots/app.md`). The app's 90 feedback cases currently have no second engine. Marketing sections run in both Chrome and WebKit.

## To do

- Find the cause. Candidates: one long-lived WebKit context accumulating pages or audio contexts, service workers, or the fixture server's keep-alive and socket limits. A fresh context per N cases, or per case, is a cheap first test.
- Make the run bounded: a per-case timeout, plus a job `timeout-minutes` so a hang fails fast instead of holding the runner.
- Re-enable WebKit for app-flows in `hig-quality.yml`.

## Acceptance

- Three consecutive local and CI runs of app-flows in WebKit pass all 90 cases.
- CI runs app-flows in Chrome and WebKit, and the job has a timeout.

Part of #110.

Found while moving the bloxwap/monorepo mobile toast stack onto HIG `Toast` for #110 (candidate `0.1.0-candidate.shab2f7740c`).

## Observed (iOS Simulator, iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0; Android emulator, font scale 2.0)

Each `Notice` renders as an `Alert`: a 24/30 `Heading` for the message plus a 48dp Dismiss `Button` in a padded `Surface`. At the default text size, three notices fill about a third of the screen. At AXXXL the third notice's Dismiss sat below the bottom edge, and `Toast` does not scroll. The app now wraps the stack in a `ScrollView` capped at 60% of the window (screenshots `toasts.png` / `toasts-scrolled.png` under `large-text-axxxl/` in the monorepo evidence).

Smaller points:

- `Notice` has no title/description split. The app joins them as `"{title}. {description}"`, so the description is set as a heading.
- Every notice gets Dismiss; there is no non-closable notice.
- There is no auto-dismiss contract. The host must time lifetimes itself.

## Ask

A compact toast presentation:

- body-size message, optional description line
- optional `closable`
- `maxHeight`/scroll behaviour for large text

Optionally, a documented lifetime prop.

body:
Found while migrating the bloxwap/monorepo mobile language picker for #110 (candidate `0.1.0-candidate.shab2f7740c`).

## Problem

`RadioGroup` (native) takes `options: {value, label: string}`. It paints each label in the provider's face for the current locale. A language list needs more per option:

- the native name in its own script's registered face (한국어 in the Korean companion while the app runs in English; Han in the SC companion)
- a second line with the translated name
- `accessibilityLanguage` per option, so VoiceOver/TalkBack pronounce the native name

Also, HIG Text detects the script of a run for letter spacing (`detectScript`) but not for the registered family. `fontFamilies` is chosen by the provider locale, so a Hangul run in an English provider falls back to the OS face.

bloxwap/monorepo therefore builds the picker from HIG Heading/Text/Surface/Separator, `useControllable` and `useColors`, with its own rows. On the Android emulator, TalkBack double tap on those rows (react-native-gesture-handler Pressable) did not select until the rows handled the `activate` accessibility action.

## Ask

- `RadioGroup` options with an optional `description` and `lang` (sets `accessibilityLanguage`, picks the registered face for that script).
- Or: HIG Text routes `fontFamilies` by detected script (a `fontFamiliesByScript` provider option).

Found while migrating the bloxwap/monorepo mobile account sheet for #110 (candidate `0.1.0-candidate.shab2f7740c`).

## Problem

The account sheet is a Gorhom bottom sheet (ui-native `Sheet`) hosting a card stack. Each card has its own header with a back button, its own detent (`snapPoints` change per card, flush top/bottom), nested scroll views, and an overlay handle. Neither HIG option can host it:

- `Sheet` / `Dialog` is a centred `Modal`.
- `GestureSheet` always renders `Heading` + description + children + a Close `Button` inside one `BottomSheetScrollView`, with fixed `snapPoints` and `enableDynamicSizing={false}`. Nested scroll views and `flex: 1` card bodies collapse inside its scroll view. Each card would get a second title and an extra Close action.

So the account sheet container stays on ui-native in bloxwap/monorepo. Only its cards' actions moved to HIG Button (behind `EXPO_PUBLIC_HIG_PILOT`).

## Ask

A content mode for `GestureSheet`:

- visually hidden or caller-rendered title (still the accessible name and the focus target on open)
- no built-in Close (the host supplies back/close)
- children rendered without the wrapping scroll view
- `snapPoints` that may change while open

Keep the existing focus return, Android back, reduced-motion and backdrop behaviour.

Found while migrating bloxwap/monorepo mobile readouts to HIG for #110 (candidate `0.1.0-candidate.shab2f7740c`).

## Problem

`NumberReadout` and `AnimatedNumberReadout` (`@bloxwap/hig-native/data`, `/animated-number`) take no `style`, typography or colour role, and no `testID`. They always render HIG Text at 16/24 in the provider's 400 face with the `text` role colour.

Host readouts whose colour or size carries meaning cannot move to them without losing that meaning:

- PnL readouts (trade history, position cards) are green or pink by sign.
- The live chart price pill takes the direction colour.
- The trade top bar shows equity and price in the mono semibold face at 20px.

In bloxwap/monorepo the account equity pill, asset price pill and demo token balance moved anyway (behind `EXPO_PUBLIC_HIG_PILOT`). They lose the mono face and 20px size, and the call-site style lays out only a wrapper `View`. The coloured readouts stay on the app's NumberFlow reels: live chart pill, position rail, trade history, market picker, trade detail, wallet and position cards.

## Ask

- Add a typography hook that keeps the formatting and accessibility contract: a `tone` role (`positive`/`negative`/`muted`, like `Alert`'s `tone`) plus a size/weight variant or a constrained `style`.
- Pass `testID` through.

Evidence (iOS Simulator / Android emulator): the monorepo PR linked from #110, `docs/hig/evidence/native-app/hig110/` (`trade-readouts`).

## Outcome

Track the upstream SFX and Haptic API gaps that HIG works around, so they are not lost when the HIG feature issues close.

This is the `upstream-feedback-gaps` entry in `planning/release-blockers.json` (status: partial).

## Gaps

- **@bloxwap/sfx:** there is no per-root voice handle or cancellation API, so HIG cannot cancel one in-flight cue without stopping others. #22 documents the adapter workaround.
- **@bloxwap/haptic:** there is no imperative async iOS haptic API. iOS web haptics depend on a physical-tap target, and #22 documents the constraint.
- **Native sound adapter dispatch latency:** the HIG native sound adapter dispatched cues much slower than the product app's pre-loaded players. bloxwap/monorepo#4540 measured 95th percentiles of 47–52 ms on the iOS Simulator and 223–595 ms on the Android emulator, against about 1–3 ms for the app's players. These are JavaScript dispatch timings, not speaker latency. The adapter should reuse pre-loaded players.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upstream issues or PRs exist in bloxwap/sfx and bloxwap/haptic and are linked here.
- [ ] Once the upstream APIs exist, HIG adopts them and removes the documented workarounds.
- [ ] The native sound adapter dispatch p95 stays within a one-frame (16 ms) budget on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator, with a test-backed measurement. Physical latency stays in #55.

## Outcome

Publish the HIG v1 packages to npm: `@bloxwap/hig-tokens`, `@bloxwap/hig-contracts`, `@bloxwap/hig-react`, `@bloxwap/hig-native` and `@bloxwap/hig-feedback`. Consumers can then install them from the registry instead of checked-in candidate tarballs.

Follow-up to #32. Release automation, packed-consumer gates and dry runs are done and merged. Publication has not happened.

## Current state

- `npm run release:dry-run -- --channel candidate` and `-- --channel stable-simulation` produce versioned tarballs, a changelog, a docs artifact and a provenance report (`docs/governance/release.md`, `scripts/release-dry-run.mjs`). The dry run never publishes, tags or creates a release.
- Consumers vendor candidate tarballs under `vendor/bloxwap-hig/` with checksums, for example `0.1.0-candidate.sha7c67a07c`:
  - merged: bloxwap/hyperliquid#180, bloxwap/chart#53, bloxwap/font#11, bloxwap/sfx#50, bloxwap/haptic#26
  - open: bloxwap/monorepo#4540
- **Blocker:** npm credentials are not configured on the release machine. No npm token or trusted-publishing configuration exists for the `@bloxwap` scope in this repository's CI.

## Scope

- Configure npm publishing for the `@bloxwap` scope: an org owner, and either GitHub Actions trusted publishing (OIDC provenance) or an automation token stored as a repository secret.
- Decide the first registry version (`0.1.0` or `1.0.0`) against the semver and deprecation policy in `docs/governance/release.md`.
- Add a guarded publish job that only a maintainer-approved release can trigger, reusing the dry-run artifacts and their hashes. Pass `--provenance`.
- Tag the release and create the GitHub release from the same commit as the docs.
- Open PRs in every consuming repo to replace `vendor/bloxwap-hig/*.tgz` `file:` dependencies with registry versions, and delete the vendored tarballs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The five packages are installable from npm, and their tarball hashes match the dry-run artifacts for the same commit.
- [ ] Registry provenance links each package to its source commit and CI run.
- [ ] Packed web, SSR, Next, Metro and Expo smokes pass against the registry install.
- [ ] Every consumer that vendors tarballs has a merged PR switching to the registry version, and `planning/adoption.json` records the published version.
- [ ] Remaining physical-device gates are tracked in #55 and are listed as known limitations in the release notes. They are not reported as passing.

## Outcome

Certify HIG v1 on physical iPhone and Android hardware. Software, browser, iOS Simulator and Android emulator acceptance for the issues below is met, and those issues are closed. This issue keeps the observations that only physical hardware can provide, so none of them is counted as passing.

Roadmap: #1 · Milestone: M5 · Upstream: bloxwap/haptic#9, bloxwap/haptic#7

## What has already been observed (not physical)

- **Automated / browser:** `npm run check`, packed web/SSR/Next/Metro consumers, three-engine browser and axe gates (see `evidence/` and CI).
- **iOS Simulator** (iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 26.5, Xcode 27.2) and **Android emulator** (Medium_Phone_API_35, Android 15 arm64): `evidence/native-sim/native-sim.json`, from merged #53 and the native overlay orientation fix in #54.

The Simulator has no Taptic Engine and no VoiceOver. The emulator has no vibration motor (only VibratorManager history), and TalkBack ignored adb-injected input. Neither shows how a real panel, speaker or touch surface behaves.

- [ ] **#28:** physical-device captures of the native gallery, with device and OS recorded.

- [ ] **#35:** the product app (bloxwap/monorepo#4540) on devices: VoiceOver/TalkBack swipe navigation, real sound output, silent mode, interruptions, haptic feel, real output latency, P3 colour.
- [ ] **#47:** RTL, large text and translated layouts on physical devices.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each item above has a recorded physical observation, or a dated, owner-approved exception, in `evidence/physical/`, labelled separately from automated, browser, simulator and emulator evidence.
- [ ] Every failure found on a device has its own linked issue.
- [ ] `planning/release-blockers.json` `physical-devices` is updated from the recorded results, and haptic#9 is cross-linked.

title: Physical-device certification for HIG v1

body:
Build a complete **Bloxwap-owned human interface guideline and component system** that every Bloxwap repository can apply to React web and React Native mobile interfaces, documentation, and marketing surfaces.

## Product direction

- Carry forward our existing web/mobile component design, Bloxwap Sans/Mono/Pixel fonts, brand palette and marks, geometry, and interactions. Start from evidence in current products and SDK docs.
- Use small composable components, shared tokens/behavioral contracts, and separate DOM/native renderers. Consolidate duplication while preserving intentional touch-app versus compact-Pro differences.
- Compose visual state and motion with optional Bloxwap SFX and haptic adapters. Support sound only, haptics only, both, neither, and host-owned adapters without changing the primary action.
- Prefer versioned packages with individual imports to repeated source copies; finalize names/primitive choices in the architecture task. Arbitrary shadcn compatibility, its full component catalog, a universal theme generator, and a shadcn registry/CLI are outside v1.
- Make the landing page a configuration-panel plus live-preview playground inspired by [shadcn Create](https://ui.shadcn.com/create), with Bloxwap-approved choices. Shape the catalog and component pages after [shadcn component docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components).

## Starting evidence and integration constraints

The monorepo already has [shared tokens](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/tokens), [shared web primitives](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/ui), [app-owned primitives](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/apps/app/src/components/ui), [Pro controls](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/apps/pro/src/components/ui), [native primitives](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/ui-native), and [plain CSS/UI](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/plain-ui). The audit must identify ownership and legitimate differences before extraction.

[@bloxwap/font](https://github.com/bloxwap/font/blob/main/packages/npm/README.md) provides Sans, Mono, Pixel, and script companions. Native typography requires explicit asset registration and scale mapping. Existing token docs identify web/native rem-root and color-space differences that must be preserved or changed deliberately.

The [SFX native guide](https://github.com/bloxwap/sfx/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/guides/native.mdx) provides offline WAV export for native playback. The [haptic platform guide](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/platforms.mdx) describes a React/web implementation with physical-tap iOS and browser-vibration constraints; HIG must implement an explicit RN haptics adapter. Physical-device certification is tracked upstream in [bloxwap/haptic#9](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/9). API calls and simulator tests are not evidence of tactile output.

## Execution

All 35 tasks are required for v1. **P0** marks foundational work and the first usable integrations; **P1** completes catalog coverage, guidance, and rollout. Follow each issue's direct prerequisites. Milestones group deliverables; component, feedback, docs, and quality work can proceed concurrently once their prerequisites are available.

### M1: Foundations and architecture

Audit existing Bloxwap designs; define HIG principles, architecture, tokens, fonts, layout, motion, accessibility, and brand assets.

- [ ] #2 — Inventory existing Bloxwap interfaces and define the v1 component catalog
- [ ] #3 — Write the Bloxwap HIG principles and product interaction rules
- [ ] #4 — Choose the shared package architecture and source-of-truth ownership
- [ ] #5 — Bootstrap the HIG workspace and runnable web/native consumer fixtures
- [ ] #6 — Extract semantic design tokens and generate web/native color outputs
- [ ] #7 — Integrate Bloxwap fonts and define cross-platform typography
- [ ] #8 — Define spacing, geometry, density, and adaptive layout rules
- [ ] #9 — Specify motion and gesture behavior with reduced-motion alternatives
- [ ] #10 — Establish accessibility, localization, and platform behavior standards
- [ ] #11 — Standardize Bloxwap brand marks and icon usage across web/native

### M2: React and React Native components

Implement the Bloxwap component contracts with React DOM and React Native renderers, platform behavior, chart integration, and product recipes.

- [ ] #12 — Implement shared component contracts and platform providers
- [ ] #13 — Build Bloxwap action and surface primitives for React and RN
- [ ] #14 — Build text input and form-field primitives for React and RN
- [ ] #15 — Build selection, toggle, range, and segmented controls for React and RN
- [ ] #16 — Build dialogs, sheets, menus, and contextual overlays for React and RN
- [ ] #17 — Build navigation, discovery, and disclosure components
- [ ] #18 — Build status, notification, loading, and empty-state components
- [ ] #19 — Build structured data and financial display components
- [ ] #20 — Define chart theming and integrate @bloxwap/chart as an optional component
- [ ] #26 — Build Bloxwap product, marketing, and SDK documentation recipes

### M3: SFX and haptics

Compose semantic interaction feedback with existing Bloxwap SFX and haptic packages and explicit native adapters; support preferences and device verification.

- [ ] #21 — Define the composable sound and haptic feedback contract
- [ ] #22 — Integrate @bloxwap/sfx and @bloxwap/haptic with React web components
- [ ] #23 — Build the React Native SFX asset pipeline and playback adapter
- [ ] #24 — Build the React Native haptics adapter and platform capability matrix
- [ ] #25 — Implement semantic feedback presets, preference controls, and preview recipes

### M4: HIG website and documentation

Build the Bloxwap playground landing page, component catalog, React/React Native previews, and complete human interface guideline documentation.

- [ ] #27 — Build the Bloxwap HIG documentation shell and component catalog
- [ ] #29 — Build the interactive Bloxwap playground landing page
- [ ] #28 — Build component previews, code examples, and a native example gallery
- [ ] #30 — Write the complete HIG, component usage, installation, and migration documentation

### M5: Release and repository adoption

Publish consumable packages, establish quality gates, migrate product and SDK documentation surfaces, and maintain an organization-wide adoption matrix.

- [ ] #32 — Publish versioned HIG packages and automate releases
- [ ] #31 — Add cross-platform quality, accessibility, visual, and size gates
- [ ] #33 — Migrate the Bloxwap app, Pro, and marketing web surfaces to HIG
- [ ] #34 — Migrate Hyperliquid, Chart, Font, SFX, and Haptic documentation to HIG
- [ ] #35 — Migrate the React Native application to HIG and verify iOS/Android behavior
- [ ] #36 — Complete organization-wide adoption and establish HIG governance

## v1 completion criteria

- [ ] The audited component catalog and all foundational HIG chapters are complete, with no orphaned component or unplanned platform gap.
- [ ] React DOM and RN have actual supported implementations/native alternatives, a versioned platform matrix, and passing clean consumer builds.
- [ ] Brand tokens, fonts, icons, units, native color spaces, density, motion, accessibility, and locale behavior are consistent and traceable to one source.
- [ ] Optional sound/haptic composition honors user preferences, event cancellation, unsupported hardware, and deduplication; iOS/Android device evidence matches support claims.
- [ ] Landing playground, component docs, examples/API references, and installation/migration guides work with the shipped artifacts and code examples.
- [ ] Versioned packages/releases and meaningful web/native/SSR/Metro/visual/accessibility/size gates are in place; duplicated source/assets and consumer footprint improvements are measured.
- [ ] bloxwap.app, bloxwap.pro, bloxwap.com, the RN app, and Hyperliquid/Chart/Font/SFX/Haptic docs have migrated surfaces and linked validation.
- [ ] Every active Bloxwap repository has an applicability/adoption decision and migration status, with owners and dated exceptions where needed; governance prevents new design drift.

## Design references

- [Hyperliquid](https://github.com/bloxwap/hyperliquid/tree/main/apps/docs)
- [Chart](https://github.com/bloxwap/chart/tree/main/apps/docs)
- [Font](https://github.com/bloxwap/font/tree/main/apps/docs)
- [Sfx](https://github.com/bloxwap/sfx/tree/main/apps/docs)
- [Haptic](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/tree/main/apps/docs)
- [Appsite](https://bloxwap.app)
- [Prosite](https://bloxwap.pro)
- [Comsite](https://bloxwap.com)
